newsitem.title: UK: United News to merge printing plants.
newsitem.headline: United News to merge printing plants.

text.p: United News & Media Plc said its United Newspapers subsidiary plans to merge its two main printing plants and will, as a result, take an exceptional charge of 32 million stg.

The 32 million stg one-off charge reflects the total cost of the merger of the printing activity together with the costs to be incurred in reorganising the Express Newspapers publishing activities and related matters. The charge will be taken against operating profit by United in its full year.
United News said it expects the pay back on the one-off cost will be achieved over the next three years.
The company plans to merge the two main printing plants serving Express Newspapers Plc and United Provincial Newspapers in the north of England.
Presses currently located at Express Printers in Manchester will be transferred to the United Provincial site at Broughton near Preston.

The merger will take about two years to complete, with the first moves expected to occur early in 1997. The changes will create a significant number of new jobs at Preston but will result in redundancies at Manchester, the company said.
United News said it is hoped that many employees now at Manchester will accept job offers at the Broughton plant.
